usageNotes: Use this endpoint to authenticate a user and obtain a PVE ticket (cookie) and CSRFPreventionToken required for all subsequent authenticated API calls. The `password` field also accepts an existing valid ticket for ticket renewal. Note that API tokens (`allowtoken: false`) cannot be used to call this endpoint — it requires real user credentials.

examples.summary: Authenticate as the root@pam user to get a session ticket

tips: The returned `ticket` value must be sent as a cookie named `PVEAuthCookie` on subsequent requests.
The `CSRFPreventionToken` must be included as the `CSRFPreventionToken` request header on all POST/PUT/DELETE requests; GET requests do not require it.
Tickets are valid for 2 hours; re-call this endpoint before expiry (or pass the old ticket as `password`) to renew without re-entering credentials.
If the user has TOTP/WebAuthn configured, the first call returns a `ticket` prefixed with `PVECHALLENGE:` — pass it back as `tfa-challenge` along with the OTP code to complete login.
The `realm` param lets you separate the realm from the username; otherwise include it directly as `user@realm` in `username`.
Use the optional `path` + `privs` params to verify a ticket AND check a privilege in a single round-trip instead of a separate ACL check.
